speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly how your cough feels, and does it produce any mucus? If so, what color is the mucus and how much do you cough up? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Right lower lobe consolidation consistent with a possible pneumonia. No pleural effusion noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: That confirms a lung infection; have you been experiencing any fever, chills, or night sweats alongside this cough? Do you have any medical history of heart disease or recent travel that might explain this?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have had no fever, chills, or night sweats, and I do not have any history of heart disease. I also haven't been traveling anywhere recently; I just live here with my spouse and garden in my spare time. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the X-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation but you lack fever or systemic symptoms, this is unusual for typical bacterial pneumonia; have you recently taken antibiotics, and do you smoke or have a history of asthma? DIAGNOSIS READY: Aspiration Pneumonia
